item.title: Israeli forces shoot Palestinian child, detain 2 in West Bank raids
item.description: Israeli forces shot and wounded a Palestinian child and detained two men during raids in the occupied West Bank late Saturday, Palestinian media reported. Palestine TV said the child was shot in the foot during a raid near the Kafr Saba neighborhood in the northern city of Qalqilya. The official Wafa news agency separately reported that troops detained a man at his home in Hebron and another in Taybeh, east of Ramallah. The second man’s vehicle was also seized. In Hebron, soldiers raided another house, confined the family to one room and ransacked the property. item.title: Israeli troops storm school, raid homes in southern Syria
item.description: Israeli troops stormed a school on Saturday and raided several homes in southern Syria, state media reported. Al-Ikhbariya TV said a patrol of 14 military vehicles entered the village of Al-Samadaniyah al-Gharbiyah in Quneitra province. Soldiers forced open the school’s gate and entered the grounds. The report provided no details on casualties or arrests. Israeli troops set up a temporary checkpoint earlier Saturday in northern Quneitra. Another unit advanced toward Wadi al-Raqad in western Daraa. Palestinian church committee urges aid for flood-hit Gaza
item.description: A Palestinian presidential committee on Saturday urged churches worldwide to provide aid to the Gaza Strip and help protect its places of worship as heavy rain battered displaced families already struggling without safe shelter, Anadolu reports. In an urgent appeal, the Higher Presidential Committee for Church Affairs in Palestine called for food, drinking water, medicines, tents and winter supplies, with a priority for children, infants, the elderly and the sick. About 950,000 displaced people are living in flood-prone areas, including more than 400,000 at high risk, said the committee. It said rainwater seeped into Gaza City’s historic Saint Porphyrius Greek Orthodox Church, underscoring the need to protect places of worship and repair damage to religious and historic sites. item.title: IRGC says three tankers ablaze in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
IRGC says three tankers ablaze in Strait of Hormuz

Iran's Revolutionary Guards reports that “three rogue oil tankers traveling an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz have been hit by explosions and severe fires”.

The IRGC said that the tankers were ablaze because they turned off their navigation and identification systems and because of the aggression of the American invading military".

It warned that: “The Iranian regulations for the Strait of Hormuz have been repeatedly announced to all vessels, and defiance of these regulations … will have no other fate".

Palestinian journalist and activist freed from Israeli police custody after five-day detention
item.description:
Palestinian journalist and activist freed from Israeli police custody after five-day detention

The Palestinian journalist and activist Abed Abu Shehadeh has been freed following five days in Israeli police custody.

Abu Shehadeh was arrested on Wednesday after Israeli police and Shin Bet officials raided his Jaffa home on the pretext of "contact with a foreign agent".

He told Arab48 that his arrest was "politically motivated".

“We must not be afraid. We are on the right path, fighting for equality and justice for all," he said.

item.title: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards say 2 oil tankers hit mines, caught fire near Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said late Saturday that two oil tankers were burning after striking naval mines in and near the Strait of Hormuz, Anadolu reports. The IRGC said the tankers switched off their navigation and positioning systems and attempted to use an unauthorized route. It accused both vessels of multiple violations, saying one was hit east of the strait and the other inside it. Earlier on Saturday, the US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM) said an American aircraft disabled a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman after repeated attempts to breach the US naval blockade of Iran. item.title: Watch: Footage shows Palestinian families struggling to drain rainwater from their tents
item.description:
Watch: Footage shows Palestinian families struggling to drain rainwater from their tents

Footage shot by photojournalist Mahmoud Hamda shows displaced Palestinian families wading through the rain water that has inundated their tents.

Young children can be seen ankle deep in murky water, trying to sweep it with brooms from their makeshift homes.

Heavy rains in the territory have deluged around 70,000 tents. Scarce aid- particularly shelter materials like tent poles and mobile homes- has left Palestinians exposed to the elements for the fourth winter in a row.

Israel's razing of Gaza's infrastructure- including water and sewage networks- and its healthcare system, means that Palestinians are particularly vulnerable to the onset of disease.

IRGC dismisses new US plan to tighten economic pressure on Iran as 'wordplay'
item.description:
IRGC dismisses new US plan to tighten economic pressure on Iran as 'wordplay'

The US cannot achieve its goals of blockading Iran's economy and shutting its trade routes because Tehran has made preparations and communicates closely with neighbours, a Revolutionary Guards spokesperson was quoted as saying on Sunday.

Hossein Mohebbi was reacting to the US military's Task Force Iron Gate, launched to help crack down on Tehran's movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material over its land borders and through the Caspian Sea.

"The Iron Gate plan is merely a wordplay, the Americans cannot achieve their objectives of imposing severe economic pressure to cause economic collapse in Iran through this approach," Mohebbi told the semi-official Fars news agency.

Reporting by Reuters
